title: Active vs Passive Immunity & Vaccine Biotechnology
topic: Natural vs Artificial Immunity, Colostrum, ATS, & 1st/2nd/3rd Gen Vaccines
quickSummary: Active immunity: host produces own antibodies upon antigen exposure (Natural: infection; Artificial: vaccination). Passive immunity: pre-formed antibodies transferred (Natural: maternal IgG across placenta, IgA in colostrum; Artificial: Anti-Tetanus Serum ATS, anti-snake venom). Vaccine generations: 1st gen (whole killed/attenuated), 2nd gen (recombinant subunit e.g. Hepatitis B in yeast), 3rd gen (DNA/mRNA).

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Active immunity involves active antibody synthesis and long-lasting memory generation by host B-cells (natural via recovery, artificial via vaccines). Passive immunity involves direct transfer of pre-formed antibodies for immediate, transient protection (natural via maternal IgG/IgA, artificial via ATS). Vaccines span 1st, 2nd (recombinant yeast Hepatitis B), and 3rd generations.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 5.1 Active vs. Passive Immunity Comparison

| Category | Definition | Natural Example | Artificial Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Active Immunity** | Host mounts its own immune response and synthesizes antibodies upon exposure to living or dead antigens; slow to develop but generates long-lasting **immunological memory**. | Recovery from natural infection (*Chickenpox, Measles*) | **Vaccination** (*BCG, MMR, OPV, Hepatitis B*) |
| **Passive Immunity** | Ready-made, pre-formed antibodies are directly administered to a non-immune individual; provides immediate protection but **generates NO immunological memory** (short-lived). | Maternal **$\text{IgG}$** across placenta to fetus; Secretory **$\text{IgA}$** in early **Colostrum** breast milk | **Anti-Tetanus Serum (ATS)**; Anti-Rabies Serum; Anti-snake venom |

### 5.2 Vaccine Generations in Biotechnology
1. **First-Generation Vaccines**:
   - Whole-pathogen formulations.
   - *Live Attenuated*: Pathogen weakened by serial subculturing (e.g., **BCG** against tuberculosis, **Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV - Sabin)**, **MMR** against measles/mumps/rubella).
   - *Inactivated / Killed*: Pathogen killed with heat or formalin (e.g., **Injectable Polio Vaccine (IPV - Salk)**, Rabies, Cholera, Pertussis).
2. **Second-Generation Vaccines (Recombinant Subunit)**:
   - Antigenic proteins produced via recombinant DNA technology in host organisms.
   - *Example*: **Hepatitis B Vaccine** produced in transgenic yeast (*Saccharomyces cerevisiae*) by expressing the Hepatitis B surface antigen ($	ext{HBsAg}$).
3. **Third-Generation Vaccines (Nucleic Acid Vaccines)**:
   - DNA or mRNA constructs that instruct host cells to produce the viral antigen directly (e.g., mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccines).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Toxoid Vaccines
conceptBreakdown.title: Toxoid Vaccines
conceptBreakdown.content: Toxoids are chemically inactivated bacterial exotoxins (using formaldehyde) that lose their pathogenicity while retaining immunogenicity, such as Tetanus Toxoid (TT) and Diphtheria Toxoid (in DPT).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Herd Immunity Threshold
conceptBreakdown.title: Herd Immunity Threshold
conceptBreakdown.content: Herd immunity occurs when a critical proportion of the population is vaccinated (threshold Qc = 1 - 1/R0), interrupting pathogen transmission chains and protecting unvaccinated vulnerable individuals.
